name: Leaning Cable Lateral Raise (Foot Forward Stance)
description: The leaning cable lateral raise with foot forward stance uses a split/lunge stance with the same-side foot as the working arm placed forward, stabilizing the lean angle differently than the common same-side foot braced on the cable unit. This stance variation allows a more consistent lean angle throughout the set and provides a stable base from which to isolate the lateral deltoid through a fuller range than the standard leaning version.

execution.starting_position: Stand beside a low cable pulley. Take a split stance — the foot closer to the cable goes forward. Hold the low cable handle with the far hand, leaning slightly away from the cable.
execution.setup_instructions: Foot forward on the working-arm side provides stable counterbalance to the lean. Set the cable to the lowest position.
steps: Step 1: Establish the split-stance lean, working hand holding the cable below hip level.
Step 2: Raise the working arm out and up to shoulder height.
Step 3: Hold 1 second at the top.
Step 5: Complete all reps then switch sides.
common_mistakes: Shifting the torso during the raise — the lean angle is fixed
Using the non-working hand to assist balance inappropriately
safety_considerations: Light load — isolation exercise for medial deltoid development
Ensure the foot placement gives stable balance before beginning
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arm at side to shoulder height.
coaching_cues: Lean is set before you start — don't drift
Raise to shoulder height — stop there
